video_title: Ray Allen: We HAVE To Talk To Our Kids

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the historical struggle of Black people in America
quotes.excerpt: We're literally our ancestors' wildest dreams.
quotes.quote: We're literally our ancestors' wildest dreams because what we get to do, what we do, how we move, what we have in our pockets, what we drive, where we can go to restaurants—you just walk in a restaurant, you need a table for two. Back then, where did the colors sit? Where did we? So that's why I always have to remember how my dad raised me or didn't raise me, or what he did for me and didn't do for me. What did he know to teach me? And that's why I said you show them grace, because we grew up in an America where we have more equality. We're literally our ancestors' wildest dreams.

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the history of police brutality and systemic racism
quotes.excerpt: Radio Raheem was killed back in Bed-Stuy a long time ago.
quotes.quote: We just talked about it and it hit the forefront with George Floyd. But Radio Raheem was killed back in Bed-Stuy a long time ago. And there was no reckoning then because they looked at him like he was just some knucklehead playing his music too loud. But the cops should have went to jail and I bet you they didn't go to jail. And then when we loot in that neighborhood in Bed-Stuy, they're just saying you guys are tearing your own neighborhoods up.

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the hypocrisy of the Declaration of Independence
quotes.excerpt: The Declaration of Independence, which was written in 1776, said we the people. That had nothing to do with us.
quotes.quote: You can't sit here and tell me that the Declaration of Independence, which was written in 1776, said we the people. That had nothing to do with us. We weren't the people. All men were created equal. You didn't really mean that about us. That was a lie. What men were you talking about? And the people don't even realize that because for us to sit here and talk about it, because if you ask any white person right now where black people treated equally in 1940, they would check their head and say no.

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the historical revisionism of January 6th
quotes.excerpt: Right now they're trying to say that January 6th didn't happen, it was a peaceful protest.
quotes.quote: Right now they're trying to say that January 6th didn't happen, it was a peaceful protest. And everybody's litigating it, but in 10 years from now you look back and be like, those people stormed the Capitol. You can't, this is what it is. We got the footage and now the talking heads can't sit back and try to convince us that we seen something different. Because history, when we look back, it compounds everything that took place and it says this is who Trump was. He was a racist, he was a narcissist, he was a misogynist, he was a megalomaniac, he wanted to be a dictator. All these things that he is aren't good for America and specifically aren't good for black people.

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the removal of DEI and affirmative action
quotes.excerpt: In academics and education they just got rid of affirmative action, they got rid of DEI.
quotes.quote: In academics and education they just got rid of affirmative action, they got rid of DEI. You look at any cabinet in America, very few black people. So you can say to us, hey, you can play basketball, you do all these things, but you can deny us seats at the table. You can deny us opportunity to get into Ivy League schools. That's why they wanted to get rid of all DEI policies because now there are more black and brown people that are being removed from being able to have access to get into places.

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the need to end divisiveness among Black people
quotes.excerpt: We have to stop with the chatter and the divisiveness amongst each other, blacks.
quotes.quote: We have to stop with the chatter and the divisiveness amongst each other, blacks. I 100% agree. I think that's the biggest thing that pisses me off about us. So, and think about it. Athletes, NFL guys, basketball guys, oh, look what so and so said about this guy. You never hear that in hockey. We're always selling clicks and bait and all this stuff and it's like we're at each other's throats. Why are we not celebrating each other? Why are we not helping each other?
